analysis.title: Huang out to dry?
key_insights: The Nvidia board is meeting to discuss removing Jensen Huang as CEO after reports of an alleged affair with a woman described as a Chinese spy, another with a co-worker, and allegations the firm lobbied for and supplied China with chips despite export controls. Rabobank says the US equity market is heavily weighted to AI and AI to Nvidia, so this creates serious turbulence.

Elon Musk floated hiring Huang if he is fired. The Australian Financial Review is cited as saying Huang's personal life could throw the global chip trade into chaos, and the affair is described as a counterintelligence nightmare given his close links to Trump.

The export-control defiance, which some suggest involved Commerce Secretary Lutnick, is likely to be scrutinised by the Democratic-majority Congress. Sales of US chips to middleman states may also be examined.

If the US decision to ignore chip sales to China was a geoeconomic bribe to secure Chinese rare earths and help in geopolitics, Rabobank says things could become far more turbulent. Yttrium in Japan is up nine-fold this year as Chinese shipments slowed.

The APEC summit in Shenzhen is next week and Nikkei Asia frames it as Xi Jinping's 'new Yalta' moment. Rabobank asks whether it brings escalation or de-escalation across East Asia, the Iran War, the Ukraine War and Cuba.

US-led Russia-Ukraine peace talks ended with a prisoner swap and no diplomatic breakthrough. Russia struck Kyiv with ballistic missiles hours after the talks ended, and the US is reportedly realising Europe must be in the next round.

The EU is blacklisting another 145 Russia-linked targets, including 50 banks. Russian crude prices are jumping in China and India on higher demand, and Rabobank says the limits of economic warfare are clear if the EU does not sanction those two countries.

NATO is shifting to prioritise fighting Russia over missions abroad. Germany unveiled a potential replacement for Palantir targeting systems and its army will stop using Chinese drones. France is questioning Germany's plans for missile strikes on Russia while Paris could extend its nuclear umbrella to the EU.

The UK deferred defence spending again, and right-wing press is pressing PM Burnham to restore Cold War levels. Hoax bomb threats hit thousands of schools in Italy, Scotland and Ireland, which Rabobank cites as cheap grey-zone disruption with expensive economic effects.

On Iran, VP Vance is reportedly considering direct talks with hard-liner Mohsen Rezai, while Trump privately criticises the June MoU and wants 'total victory'. New Chief of Staff Miller reportedly prefers an indefinite economic blockade, which needs help from reluctant neighbours.

Tehran says Hormuz will 'never return' to pre-war status. Saudi oil production has rebounded close to prewar levels, which Rabobank reads as Iran's crude leverage shrinking over time unless it escalates further. Tehran has threatened to bomb European air bases used by the US.

Rabobank's base case is escalation on Iran and it does not yet see a sustainable path to de-escalation. Israeli caretaker PM Netanyahu is reportedly being warned by the IDF chief and by Eisenkot against ill-advised military action.

Australia's November inflation expectations stayed at 5.3%, more than double the RBA's mid-point target. The UK Q3 GDP, US home sales, weekly jobless claims, the US federal budget balance and a speech by ECB President Lagarde are due today.

market_movers.rationale: The board is discussing removing CEO Huang over alleged affairs and export-control allegations. Rabobank flags turbulence for an equity market concentrated in AI and Nvidia, and a possible congressional probe, but gives no rating or target.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Unchanged and more than double the RBA's mid-point target, which keeps inflation pressure on the RBA.

tension_points.bull_case: De-escalation: Vance is considering direct talks with hard-liner Mohsen Rezai, and Saudi oil production has rebounded close to prewar levels, which reduces Iran's leverage in crude.
tension_points.bear_case: Escalation: Trump wants 'total victory', Miller prefers an indefinite blockade, Tehran says Hormuz will never return to pre-war status and has threatened European air bases. Rabobank's base case is escalation.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Iran escalating further would restore its leverage in crude, as the report notes.

tension_points.bull_case: A prisoner swap took place and the US is reportedly realising Europe must join the next round of talks, which could open a diplomatic path.
tension_points.bear_case: No diplomatic breakthrough, Russian ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv hours after the talks, and the limits of EU sanctions if China and India are not targeted.
